# Message checks


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

The [scope](design/scope.ipynb) lists failure modes that code can check
by comparing a message with its triage record, with no labels needed.
This module implements them for the first task. The same checks screen
the teacher’s messages before they become training data, and score the
base and fine-tuned models, broken down by tuple.

## A record and its message

The examples use one record from the generator in
[`coffee`](01_coffee.ipynb), with a severe, a moderate and an early
item:

``` python
rec = triage(dict(problem='both', pattern='cluster', severity='severe'), random.Random(19))
rec
```

A message that keeps every rule has one paragraph per item. Each
paragraph starts with the item’s marker and its location exactly as in
the record, then a colon, then what is wrong and what to do:

``` python
msg = """🚨 Plot 1: some monitored plants in this plot have been short of water since Saturday, and no water has reached their soil since Friday. Check this plot's irrigation line today, from its start to the last plant.

⚠️ Plot 2: most sensors in this plot have sent no data since Sunday, so the plants they cover are not monitored. Check the power supply these sensors share.

👀 Plot 3, row 1: the camera at this plant has not seen its leaves since today. Check that it points at the plant and that nothing blocks its view."""
```

## Parsing

[`parse`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/edgeslm/checks.html#parse)
splits a message into paragraphs, and reads the marker, location and
text of each. Models sometimes drop the invisible variation selector
that follows ⚠ in ⚠️, so
[`parse`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/edgeslm/checks.html#parse)
accepts the marker with or without it.

### parse

``` python
def parse(
    msg:str, # A message, with one paragraph per item
)->list: # (marker, location, text) for each paragraph, or `None` for one not in that format
```

*Split `msg` into its items*

<summary>Exported source</summary>

``` python
MARKERS = dict(early='👀', moderate='⚠️', severe='🚨')
```

</details>

``` python
ps = parse(msg)
test_eq([(m, l) for m, l, _ in ps], [('🚨', 'Plot 1'), ('⚠️', 'Plot 2'), ('👀', 'Plot 3, row 1')])
ps[0]
```

    ('🚨',
     'Plot 1',
     "some monitored plants in this plot have been short of water since Saturday, and no water has reached their soil since Friday. Check this plot's irrigation line today, from its start to the last plant.")

A paragraph without a marker and a location gives `None`:

``` python
test_eq(parse("Check your farm today.\n\n⚠ Block B, drip line B1: check the line."), [None, ('⚠️', 'Block B, drip line B1', 'check the line.')])
```

## Checks

[`check`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/edgeslm/checks.html#check)
runs the checks of the scope, and returns whether each passed:

- `format`: every paragraph has a marker and a location.
- `coverage`: every item of the record has its paragraph.
- `no_invented`: every paragraph names a location from the record, and
  no location has two paragraphs.
- `severity`: each paragraph has the marker of its item’s severity.
- `no_numbers`: no digits outside the record’s locations, so no
  readings, counts or dates.
- `length`: at most `MAX_LEN` characters.
- [`amount`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/edgeslm/coffee.html#amount):
  each cluster or widespread item uses its record’s
  [`amount`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/edgeslm/coffee.html#amount)
  word.

Locations are compared without case, so that “Whole farm” at the start
of a paragraph matches `whole farm`.

Each check catches one kind of mistake. This message gives a date, says
“most” where half the sensors are flagged, marks the second item as
severe, and leaves out the third item, so it fails four checks:

``` python
bad = """🚨 Plot 1: most monitored plants in this plot have been short of water since 19 September. Check this plot's irrigation line today.

🚨 Plot 2: most sensors in this plot have sent no data since Sunday. Check the power supply these sensors share."""
res = check(rec, bad)
test_eq({k for k, v in res.items() if not v}, {'no_numbers', 'severity', 'coverage', 'amount'})
res
```

    {'format': True,
     'coverage': False,
     'no_invented': True,
     'severity': False,
     'no_numbers': False,
     'length': True,
     'amount': False}
